slot.brief: Given K for a reaction, ask K for the reversed reaction and/or multiplied stoichiometry; pure manipulation, no numbers.

stem: For the reaction N2(g) + 3 H2(g) <=> 2 NH3(g), the equilibrium constant is K. The equilibrium constant for the reaction NH3(g) <=> 1/2 N2(g) + 3/2 H2(g) is

verdicts.working: The target reaction is the reverse of the given reaction, scaled by 1/2. Reversing gives 1/K; scaling by 1/2 gives (1/K)^(1/2) = 1/√K.

working:
Original reaction: K = [NH3]^2 / ([N2][H2]^3). Reversing gives K_rev = 1/K = [N2][H2]^3 / [NH3]^2. Dividing coefficients by 2 gives K_target = (K_rev)^(1/2) = (1/K)^(1/2) = 1/sqrt(K).

Independent check: The target reaction is the reverse of the given reaction, scaled by 1/2. Reversing gives 1/K; scaling by 1/2 gives (1/K)^(1/2) = 1/√K.
solution:
Reversing a reaction changes its equilibrium constant to $1/K$, and multiplying all coefficients by $1/2$ raises it to the power $1/2$.
$$K_{\text{target}}=\left(\frac{1}{K}\right)^{1/2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt K}$$
